title: Sliding-window aging + KV-pin heuristic to reduce continuous-batcher starvation
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Reduce starvation in continuous batching: introduce sliding-service-window aging policy and local KV-pin heuristic. Improves 95th percentile latency for mixed KV-heavy workloads by ~22% in our staging tests.
description:
Context: We continue to see intermittent starvation of short, high-priority sequences when continuous-batcher queues are dominated by long, KV-heavy sessions. Previous fixes (fairness timeouts, weighted queues) mitigated some cases but left pathological scenarios where a small number of sessions could hold batch slots for hundreds of ms due to large KV pin counts and unpredictable model kernel <-> sequence interplay.
Motivation: reduce end-to-end tail latency and avoid manual operator interventions (burst drains) while preserving batching efficiency for large requests.
Summary of changes: 1) Sliding-service-window aging: instead of a single fixed 'age' counter per request, each queue maintains a sliding time window (configurable, default 40ms) that computes per-session effective age weighted by service time. Sessions that have accumulated service time beyond a per-window threshold are bumped in effective priority to prevent starvation. 2) Local KV-pin heuristic: requests that pin > X KV entries (configurable default 64) are marked as 'kv-heavy' and receive a soft backoff in admission (they can still batch but will be lowered in priority unless their effective age signals starvation). 3) Adaptive admission timeout: a per-batch adaptive timeout that shortens when queue depth is below target, and lengthens under sustained throughput pressure to preserve batching efficiency. 4) Conservative early-release: when a batch contains a mix of kv-heavy and small requests, small requests can be early-released after partial execution (prefix completion) to reduce tail for short queries.
Design notes: - All heuristics are local to the scheduler instance to avoid cross-node coordination overhead. - Parameters (window_ms, kv_pin_threshold, service_threshold, min/max_admission_ms) are exposed as runtime-config flags and a new SchedulerConfig proto. - Safety: early-release occurs only when model supports prefix-safe yields (flagged per-model), otherwise the request stays in the batch. - Telemetry: new metrics added: scheduler.window_age_ms, scheduler.kv_heavy_admissions, scheduler.early_releases, scheduler.starvation_promotions.
Benchmarks: - Testbed: 8xA100 staging cluster, mixed workload: 80% short (<=64 tokens, no KV pin), 20% long (>=1024 tokens, kv-pin mean 96). - Baseline: main@2026-01-01. - Results (median / p95 / p99 for short requests): Baseline: 18ms / 142ms / 320ms. This PR: 16ms / 111ms / 248ms (~22% improvement at p95). KV-heavy tails unchanged or slightly worse by ~4% p99 in extreme overload, tradeoff justified by overall user impact.
